profile_text.body:
Cerence Inc. is a public company traded under the ticker CRNC, with CIK 0001768267, headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts. On its website the company describes itself as delivering conversational and agentic AI-powered user experiences for automotive and beyond, built on CaLLM, which it calls its family of language models. It says this work is meant to enable natural, multimodal and safe interactions, and that it is moving to advance generative AI and large language model-powered innovation that it expects to be central to the automotive and transportation user experience.

Among the products the site describes is Cerence Emergency Vehicle Detection, or EVD, which the company says is already deployed in production vehicles. It detects and localizes more than 1,500 emergency sirens across nearly 50 countries, identifying approaching emergency vehicles from more than 300 meters away with interior microphones and beyond 800 meters when paired with exterior microphones. The site also describes dynamic speech enhancement for multi-seat in-car environments, which lets passengers in different zones make requests at the same time. Cerence reported third quarter results with revenue up 12% year over year, connected services revenue up 20% year over year, and operating cash flow of $20M supporting a first-ever share repurchase program. Other site material covers work with Microsoft on Zero Trust architecture for in-car assistants, credited to Kaivan Karimi of Cerence AI and Frank Kaleck of Microsoft, and a demonstration by Timo Matheja and Stefan Hamerich.

The company's litigation exposure is recorded in Massachusetts, with 187 entries.
